 This Writ Petition Coming On For Preliminary

Following:-
 Order
Sri.H.C.Shivaramu, learned counsel for the petitioner.

Mr.M.Vinod Kumar, learned Additional Government Advocate for the respondent Nos.1 to 3.
2.
The petition is admitted for hearing.
With consent of the learned counsel for the parties, the same is heard finally.

3. In this petition, the petitioner inter alia seeks a writ of certiorari for quashment of notice / order dated 01.08.2017 issued by the respondent No.1 as well as writ of certiorari issued by the respondent No.2 dated 24.10.2017 contained in Annexure-D.
4.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the petition briefly stated are that the petitioner No.1 is a trust which has been formed with an object to run the educational institutions and to start hospital and health centres with the assistance of the Government and to install water plant to cater to the water problems faced by general public.
The petitioner used to supply water by levying charges of `5/- for 20 litres of purified drinking water.

The petitioner received a notice from the designated officer by which the petitioner was asked to close down the water unit within 7 days and to get the ISI certificate failing which suitable action shall be taken against the petitioner.
The petitioner submitted a reply on 04.08.2017.

Thereafter, by an order dated 24.10.2017 issued by the respondent No.2, the electricity supplied to the premises of the petitioner was stopped on the ground that there Sree Lakshmi Venkateshwara vs The Designated Officer on 12 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5028739/
2 was a direction by the Designated Officer of Food and Civil Supply to stop the supply of electricity to the water unit run by the petitioner - Trust as the petitioners had failed to obtain the ISI certificate and had also not obtained SSA license.

sentences.text: Thereafter a representation was submitted on 01.11.2017 to the Deputy Commissioner.
However, the aforesaid representation failed to invoke any response.
In the aforesaid background, the petitioners have approached this Court.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioners, while inviting the attention of this Court to Regulation 2.10.8 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011,
submitted that since the petitioner - Trust is not selling the packaged drinking water, therefore, the petitioners are not required to obtain ISI certificate under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 6. On the other hand, learned Additional Government Advocate, while placing reliance on the Division Bench decision of this Court in 'LOCHAMESH B. HUGAR Vs. UNION OF INDIA AND OTHERS' (2013) 2 KLJ 643, submitted that the petitioner - Trust is required to obtain the ISI certificate under the Act as the expression 'packaged drinking water' include the water derived from surface or underground or sea water which is subjected to specified terms mentioned in Clause 2.10.8.

entities.text: LOCHAMESH B. HUGAR Vs. UNION OF INDIA AND OTHERS' (2013) 2 KLJ 643
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, even if the petitioner - Trust does not sell the water in packaged form, still it is required to obtain ISI certificate under the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986.

Learned Additional Government Advocate has also referred to an order dated 27.06.2018 passed by the learned Single Judge of this Court in W.P.Nos.14176-80/2018 and 14638/2018.
7.
I have considered the submissions made by learned counsel on both sides and have perused the record.

It is pertinent to mention here that the Division Bench in LOCHAMESH B.HUGAR, supra was dealing with Clause 2.10.8 of the Regulations which reads as under:
"Packaged drinking water (other than Mineral water)" means water derived from surface water or underground water or sea water which is subjected to hereinunder specified treatments, namely, decantation, filteration, combination of filteration,
aerations, filteration with membrane filter depth filter, cartridge filter, actiated carbon filteration, de-mineralisation, re- mineralisation, reverse osmosis and packed after disinfecting the water to a level that shall not lead to any harmful contamination in the drinking water by means of chemical agents or physical methods to reduce the number of micro-organisms to a level beyond scientifically accepted level for food safety of its suitability:
PROVIDED that sea water, before being subjected to the above treatments, shall be subjected to desalination and related process.

The related packaging and labeling requirements are provided in regulation 2.1.2,
2.2.1 and 2.4.5 of Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations,
2011."
8.

sentences.text:
Under the aforesaid Regulation, even if the water was not sold in a packaged condition, the person concerned was required to obtain ISI certificate under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act,

3 1986.

entities.text: Sree Lakshmi Venkateshwara vs The Designated Officer on 12 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, Clause 2.10.8 was amended with a notification which came into force w.e.f.
15.11.2016 which reads as under:
"2.10.8 Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water) - 1. Means water, other than natural mineral water that is likely to be used for human consumption and that is offered or sold in packaged form, by whatever name it may be called, offered or sold."
9. Thus, from perusal of the amended Clause 2.10.8, it is evident that if the water is not sold for human consumption in packaged form, there is no requirement of obtaining the ISI certificate.

However, the aforesaid aspect of the matter was not taken note by the learned Single Judge while deciding W.P.Nos.14176-80/2018 and 14638/2018 vide order dated 27.06.2018 and reliance was placed on the Division Bench decision of this Court in which Clause 2.10.8 as it existed at the time of decision of the writ petition was taken note of.
However, subsequently, the legal position has changed.
Therefore, neither the decision rendered by the Division Bench of this Court nor by the learned Single Judge of this Court apply to the fact situation of the case.
Since the petitioner is not selling the water in a packaged form, therefore, he is not required to obtain ISI certificate.
In view of the preceding analysis, the impugned Annexures-B, D and H are hereby quashed.
In the result, the petition is allowed.
